verifications.claim: Artemis III is currently targeted for launch in mid-2027, according to NASA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Launch Schedule Artemis III When 2027'; R2: 'slated to launch sometime in 2027'; R3: 'launched by mid-2027'
verifications.reasoning: R1 (NASA) and R2 confirm 2027 target; R3 explicitly states 'mid-2027' from NASA announcement.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will be a crewed mission aimed at testing rendezvous and docking capabilities with commercial landers in low-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Artemis III demonstration mission in low Earth orbit will test... rendezvous and docking capabilities between Orion and private commercial spacecraft'; R5: identical description
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches description of crewed LEO mission testing docking with commercial landers.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is scheduled for launch in 2027 as of April 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2 (dated April 10, 2026): 'NASA's next mission... is slated to launch sometime in 2027'
verifications.reasoning: Exactly matches timing and date context.

verifications.claim: Artemis III crew will launch on the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket in the Orion spacecraft, as reported by Space.com.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launch crew in the Orion spacecraft on top of the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'; R5: 'The Artemis III crew will launch in Orion on the SLS rocket'
verifications.reasoning: Fact directly supported; attribution to Space.com not in refs but does not contradict.

verifications.claim: Artemis III crew will dock with a commercial lander such as SpaceX’s Starship in low-Earth orbit, as reported by Space.com.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1/R5: 'test rendezvous and docking capabilities between Orion and private commercial spacecraft... one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin'; R4: 'SpaceX Starship lunar lander... for Artemis 3'
verifications.reasoning: Supports docking with SpaceX commercial lander in LEO; Starship specified in R4 context but not explicitly for LEO docking.

verifications.claim: SpaceNews and The Guardian note that this revision follows concerns over technological readiness.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3 (Guardian): 'technical glitches... too much too soon... too risky'; R4 (SpaceNews): 'potential delays in hardware... problems SpaceX has had on Starship'
verifications.reasoning: Both sources directly link revisions to tech concerns and delays.

verifications.claim: SpaceNews and The Guardian note that this revision focuses on addressing delays in the human landing system (HLS).
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R3: 'test essential technologies... space vehicles before... human moon landing'; R4: 'delays in... Starship vehicle, including the lunar lander version'
verifications.reasoning: Implies HLS issues (Starship lander) but not explicitly stated as primary focus of revision.

verifications.claim: The actual human lunar landing has been shifted to the Artemis IV mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Artemis III mission will no longer aim to land on the moon... a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states shift of landing to Artemis IV.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV is now targeted for 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'
